toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_pull_requests
toolsAdded.description: Lists the user's PR lists in Glass: PRs that need their review, their own PRs, and PRs they are reviewing, grouped by followed repository.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_queue
toolsAdded.description: Lists the PRs in the user's Queue: the PRs they lined up to review next, in order, each with the Revision Glass last saw.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_to_dos
toolsAdded.description: Lists the user's To-dos in Glass, done or not, with their notes. An image is an id and a media type; its file stays on this device.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_recent_activity
toolsAdded.description: Lists the user's most recent Activity in Glass, newest first: PRs they opened, reviewed, and commented on, and other work they did.

limit.description: How many Activities to list, at most 100.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_threads
toolsAdded.description: Lists the user's Threads, each with its repository, base branch, harness, and whether it waits for the user's answer.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_inbox
toolsAdded.description: Lists the user's Glass Inbox: what waits on them now, in four groups in this order. Stopped on you: Threads with a Permission request or Question waiting, questions from an agent outside Glass, Check-ins, and the Global chat's own waiting requests. Agent reviews to read: queued PRs whose Agent review is finished. Your pull requests: the user's own PRs with changes requested, failing checks, Review threads awaiting their reply, or ready to merge. Threads that finished: Threads whose latest Turn ended since the user last looked. Within a group, the longest waiting comes first.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_started_work
toolsAdded.description: Lists the Threads and Agent reviews you started, or Threads you messaged, oldest first: each with its state now and the user's message that asked for it. Answer how the work you started is going from this, not from the chat. Threads and reviews the user started themselves, and deleted Threads, aren't listed.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__read_thread_transcript
toolsAdded.description: Reads a Thread's most recent Turns: each message the user sent, what its agent wrote and which tools it used, and how the Turn ended. Includes Queued messages not yet delivered.

turns.description: How many of the latest Turns to read, at most 20.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__read_pull_request
toolsAdded.description: Reads a PR's title, description, changed files with their diffs, and published comments at one Revision. Pass the Revision the user means, such as the one in a message's glass_context; leave it out to read the PR as it is now.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__read_agent_review
toolsAdded.description: Reads a PR's Agent review: the latest one written, with the Revision it reviewed, and whether one is being written now or failed.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__start_agent_review
toolsAdded.description: Starts an Agent review of a PR at a Revision, as the user would from the PR. It appears beside the PR's diff once written. This returns once the review started, not when it is written, which takes minutes: read_agent_review shows its progress and result, or why it failed, such as the PR having changed since that Revision. Starting one replaces any review being written for the PR, so read_agent_review first and ask the user before replacing one.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_thread_places
toolsAdded.description: Lists where the user can start a Thread. A Thread on this device works in a copy of a Local checkout, so its repository must be one of localCheckouts. A Thread in a Sandbox works in any followed repository, in a Sandbox from one of sandboxProviders. Each place runs only the Agent harnesses listed with it.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_thread_options
toolsAdded.description: Lists the base branches and models a Thread can start with, for a repository, place, and Agent harness from list_thread_places.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__create_thread
toolsAdded.description: Creates a Thread: a named piece of work with a coding agent, on a branch of its own, made from a base branch of a repository. It starts its first Turn with the message, and appears in the user's Threads. This returns once Glass created the Thread, not when it finishes its Turn. When you are the Global chat or a Thread, Glass sends you an update when it finishes, fails, or waits on the user, so end your Turn rather than reading its transcript to wait; otherwise read_thread_transcript shows its progress. A Thread that creates one gives it its own Permission mode, and can't create one that asks the user less than it does, such as one in a Sandbox, unless it never asks either. A Thread in a Sandbox can only create Threads in a Sandbox. Choose the place, harness, base branch, and model from list_thread_places and list_thread_options, never from guesses. If this call fails without saying why, or is cut off, call list_threads before trying again rather than creating a second Thread.

baseBranch.description: The branch the Thread's branch starts from.

place.description: Where the Thread's agent works: on this device, or in a Sandbox from a provider.

harness.description: The Agent harness that runs the Thread.

model.description: A model id from list_thread_options, or null for the harness's default.

effort.description: One of the model's Efforts, or null for its default.

message.description: The Thread's first message: its task.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__send_thread_message
toolsAdded.description: Sends a message to one of the user's Threads, as the user would from the Thread. An idle Thread starts a Turn with it; a busy Thread keeps it as a Queued message and starts on it after its running Turn. This returns once Glass accepted the message, not when its agent answers. When you are the Global chat or a Thread, Glass sends you an update when it finishes, fails, or waits on the user, so end your Turn rather than reading its transcript to wait; otherwise read_thread_transcript shows its progress. A Thread can't message itself, or one that asks the user less than it does, and one in a Sandbox can only message Threads in a Sandbox. If this call fails without saying why, or is cut off, read the Thread's transcript before sending again rather than sending it twice.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__ask_user
toolsAdded.description: Asks the user one question in the Glass Inbox and returns at once with its questionId; it doesn't wait for the answer. Keep working on what doesn't depend on the answer; if nothing does, end your Turn. A Thread or the Global chat that Glass launched gets the answer as a later message with a glass_answer block naming the questionId. An agent outside Glass reads it with read_answer when it is ready for it. The user picks one of the choices or types their own answer, or sets the question aside. Ask each question with its own call.

question.description: The question, as the user should read it in the Inbox.

anyOf.description: What picking this choice means, when the label alone doesn't say.
Choices the user can pick, with distinct labels. They can still type their own answer. Omit this to ask for text only.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__read_answer
toolsAdded.description: For an agent outside Glass: reads where a question you asked with ask_user, or a Check-in you made with check_in, stands, by its id, from any of your sessions. The result is Waiting while the user hasn't answered, or SetAside when they chose not to. A question's answer is Answered (by is choice or text). A Check-in's answer is Approved or Feedback, each with the user's optional message and their Feedback notes (a file path, the side of the diff, the line range, the code they read there, their note, and whether that code changed since); or Replaced, with the id of the Check-in that replaced it when you checked in again from the same folder. Feedback asks you to change the code. Notes on an approval are guidance and ask for no more work.

id.description: The questionId ask_user returned, or the checkInId check_in returned.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__check_in
toolsAdded.description: For an agent outside Glass: asks the user to read the changes in a folder and approve them or send feedback in the Glass Inbox, under the name the user approved, and returns at once; it doesn't wait for their answer. Pass the absolute path of your working directory. Glass reads the changes itself: the working tree, staged or not and including untracked files, against where the branch forked from baseRef, frozen as they are when you call. The result is CheckedIn with the checkInId to pass read_answer when you are ready for the answer, or NoChanges when there is nothing to read. Checking in again from the same folder replaces a Check-in the user hasn't answered, and the Feedback notes they left on it carry over.

folder.description: The absolute path of the folder whose changes to read, such as your working directory.

anyOf.description: The branch or commit the changes started from. Defaults to the repository's default branch (origin/HEAD).
Plain text on what changed and where to look. Its first line titles the Check-in in the Inbox.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__wait_for_release
toolsAdded.description: Waits until Glass releases it. Call it only when the user asks you to.
